resources.string: Try another home app without losing anything. The Boox home stays one tap away, and every Boox function is listed below, so none is out of reach.
Boox home: library, notes, function bar and widgets
BooxUltimatum’s e-ink home: widgets, folders, a paged grid and low memory use
Only the Boox home is installed. Install another home app, then come back here to try it. You can always return to the Boox home.
Shizuku isn’t running. The buttons above open Android’s Default home app page, where you confirm your choice. BooxUltimatum still remembers the Boox home, so you can go back.

BooxUltimatum’s background use is restricted and it isn’t your home app, so Android may stop it between uses. The sleep screen’s refreshes, live updates and the battery log need it to keep running. Allow background use on its battery page.
Open any Boox app from here, whichever home app is in use.
Boox can stop apps you install from running in the background. Music may stop soon after you leave the player, and screen sharing may go blank.
Lifts the background restriction Boox put on apps you installed, so music, calls and screen shares can keep going after you leave the app.
Those apps may use more battery. To choose app by app, use the Restricted filter under Apps instead.
Apps you installed that Boox doesn’t let run in the background. Open one and tap Keep running in background if its music stops or its calls drop.

Boox restricts this app in the background, so playback, calls or sharing can stop soon after you leave it. Keep running in background lifts that. If the restriction comes back after a restart, tap the button again.
Can’t read the list of apps Doze never pauses. Grant system diagnostics access or start Shizuku.
Reversible changes to sleep, power, radios, the interface and privacy. Each change BooxUltimatum makes can be undone in one tap.
Block apps you choose from the network, using a VPN that runs on the tablet. It needs no root.
Turn chosen tweaks on for the night and off in the morning.
Every change records what it replaced, so you can undo it here. Nothing on this page runs in the background.
Nothing has changed yet. Tweaks you apply or undo, and actions you take on apps, appear here.
Status bar: restored to the Boox default
Android keeps Battery Saver off while the tablet is charging. It takes effect once you unplug the tablet.
How the tablet rests while the screen is off. These tweaks affect standby drain.
Everyday settings that give up some convenience to use less charge.
Background scanning that keeps Wi-Fi and Bluetooth busy even when they look turned off.
Changes that suit an e-ink screen better than Android’s phone defaults.
Block trackers and turn off Boox services you may not need.
Turns on Android’s deep sleep, called Doze, which the firmware turns off (checked on a Note Air6 C). The tablet can then pause background work while the screen is off.
Android forgets this when the tablet restarts. Apply it again afterwards.
Takes non-essential Boox apps off the list of apps that Doze never pauses. Keyboards, the home screen, NaviBall, the clock, the music player and the voice recorder stay on it.
Boox may add them back after a restart. Check this tweak again then.
Stops the Boox store, shop, transfer, factory test, AI assistant, calculator, gallery, dictionary and calibration apps from running in the background.
Turns on Android’s own Battery Saver, which limits background work and syncing for every app.
Keeps Android’s App Standby on, so apps you rarely open get fewer chances to run in the background.
Turns off Android’s automatic account sync. Accounts stop syncing on their own, and apps still sync when you open them.
Turns the screen off after 2 minutes without a touch. Undo returns to your previous timeout.
Lets the screen turn off while the tablet is charging. This turns off Android’s Stay awake developer option.
Android can scan for Wi-Fi networks to improve location, even when Wi-Fi is off. This stops it.
Stops background Bluetooth scans for nearby devices while Bluetooth is off.
Stops Wi-Fi from turning itself on near saved networks.
Turns off location services for every app, so apps that need your position can’t find it until you undo this.
Turns off Android’s window, transition and animator effects. Screens change in one clean refresh instead of a smear of frames.
Sends every app’s website lookups through AdGuard DNS, which blocks known ad and tracking domains.
Some hotel and café Wi-Fi sign-in pages won’t load until you undo this.
Turns off the Boox updater service. Nothing is uninstalled.
You won’t be told about firmware updates until you undo this.
Turn off the Boox store and shop
Turns off the Boox App Store and shop apps, so they no longer open or run. Nothing is uninstalled.
Turn off the factory test app
Turns off a production-line test tool that has no use after the tablet leaves the factory. Nothing is uninstalled.
Forces Android into deep sleep (Doze) straight away, even with the screen on, so you can test it. Stop it before normal use, because it delays notifications and syncing.
Positive while charging, as this tablet reports it

BooxUltimatum records a sample only while the tablet is awake anyway, so the log never wakes it. Turning the screen on or off, plugging in and unplugging each add a row, so standby and use stay separate. This needs nothing from you.
Search by name or package name

BooxUltimatum can’t read or change this while Shizuku isn’t running. You can still do it yourself.\nAndroid’s battery page for the app has an “Allow background usage” switch, the same one Boox turns off. Boox’s App Freeze page, which firmware 4.3 hides from its menus, lets you unfreeze the app and stop Boox from freezing new apps. You can also tap and hold the app’s icon on the Boox home screen and choose Optimize › Others.
The firmware itself exempts the app from Doze. No app can change that.
Disable hides the app and stops it from running. Nothing is uninstalled. Tap Enable to bring it back.
Removed from the Doze exemption list.
Added to the Doze exemption list.
Disabled. Tap Enable to bring it back.
